**See where memory and CPU go: the top bar's meters break the total down by agent, and show a paused agent still holding its memory. Idle agents can stop on their own, hovering an agent shows what it runs on and how fast it answers, a project's agents can follow it to another account, and the app shows what's new after an update.**

## What's new

- **Memory and CPU breakdowns.** Clicking **Host memory** or **Host CPU** in the top bar lists
  every agent, largest first, with a link to it and a Stop button. Memory shows each agent's RAM,
  swap and limit, says when a paused agent still holds its memory (pausing frees nothing), and,
  when swap is zram, what that swap really costs in RAM. CPU shows each agent's use and its cores,
  as configured and as held by **Never freeze my CPU**.
- **Auto-stop idle agents.** A new switch in **Settings → Every agent**, off by default. While
  it's on, an agent that has gone the idle time (2h by default) with no chat turn, job, waiting
  question or credential request, terminal input or recording is stopped. Paused agents count as
  idle from when they were paused. The worktree and branch are kept, and the agent's Overview says
  **Stopped after 2h idle**.
- **Agent info.** Hovering an agent row, or the new **Info** item in its right-click menu, shows
  its model, effort, context window, average tokens per second, Claude and GitHub accounts, AI
  tool, branch, state, uptime, limits, tokens and cost, and pull request.
- **Tokens per second.** The Tokens tab shows average output tokens per second in its headline,
  per agent, per model and per turn.
- **Moving a project's agents to another account.** Changing a project's Claude Code or GitHub
  account asks whether to move its agents still on the old one too; on the command line,
  `--move-agents`. A stopped or paused agent's account can be changed too, and it takes effect when
  the agent next starts. Settings says which projects don't follow the default account.
- **What's new.** The changelog is in **Settings → This app**, and opens once after the app
  updates.

## Fixes

- **A repeated credential request could be missed.** In 0.4.0 and earlier, an agent that asked
  for the same credential again right after asking could be left waiting on the first request.
- **The daemon's background account checks** could keep running after it stopped, in 0.4.0 and
  earlier.

## What went wrong

- **The credential request.** The daemon stored the request before registering who was waiting for
  its answer, so an "ask again" arriving in between found nobody to cancel. It now registers the
  waiter first.
- **The account checks.** They ran on a context of their own rather than the daemon's, so nothing
  waited for them. They are tied to the daemon's run now, and it waits for them before it stops.

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.5.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.5.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.5.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U
AgentBox-0.5.0-x64.pacman`. On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag AgentBox into Applications. On
Windows, run the installer or the portable `.exe`. See the README's
[Install](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.5.0/README.md#install) for the rest.

**Upgrading from 0.4.0:** the base image is unchanged, so there's nothing to rebuild.

## Known limitations

- **Tokens per second** only counts turns from 0.5.0 on: older turns have no duration.
- **The memory and CPU popovers** read each agent's cgroup, so an agent whose machine is stopped
  shows nothing.
- The rest are unchanged since
  [0.4.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.4.0),
  [0.3.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.3.0) and
  [0.1.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.1.0).
